fx_framing: A sprite sheet of ONE short visual-effect animation for a 2D top-down pixel-art survival game: a grid of {cols} columns and {rows} rows of equally sized square cells holding {n} frames in reading order (left to right, then the next row). Fully transparent background. Each frame sits in the middle of its own cell with a wide empty margin; nothing touches or crosses the cell borders; the effect has the same scale and the same anchor point in every frame, and consecutive frames change smoothly so they play as a fluid animation. Bold, simple, readable shapes with clear stepped cel shading (3 to 5 tones) and crisp edges, so it still reads when shrunk to a tiny pixel sprite. No text, no numbers, no labels, no grid lines, no cell borders, no background colour, no ground, no cast shadow.
fx_style: Classic 16-bit pixel-art game effect look (like Enter the Gungeon, Hyper Light Drifter, Project Zomboid effects); gritty Soviet post-apocalyptic mood, colours slightly desaturated except light-emitting parts (fire, sparks, flashes, flares) which stay bright and saturated.
